conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad we’re meeting today. I’m [Your Name], a perinatal mental-health clinician, and I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. I’ll be using a short, well-studied questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—or EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 gentle questions about the past seven days; they help us spot signs of depression or anxiety that sometimes creep up after childbirth.  

Everything you share stays between us unless you or your baby’s safety is at immediate risk, and there are no “wrong” answers. We’ll go one question at a own-pace; you can pause or clarify anything. Ready to start?

**Question 1:** In the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Lately it feels like I have to force a smile, let alone laugh. I can still chuckle if something’s really funny, but it’s not the same easy laugh I used to have—maybe once or twice this week, and even then it fades fast.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes, yes… like when the baby made that silly face during tummy-time, I laughed a little. But it’s rare—maybe one or two moments this week—and the laugh feels kind of hollow, like it disappears as soon as it comes.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like one more chore. I can still go through the motions, but there’s no spark. Maybe once or twice I thought “that might be nice,” but the feeling fades before I actually do it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

All the time. If she cries longer than usual, I’m sure it’s because I missed some cue or didn’t feed her right. When I couldn’t get her to nap yesterday I kept replaying every little thing I did, telling myself a “good mom” would’ve figured it out. I know in my head it’s not always my fault, but the thoughts just keep coming.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… pretty often. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly my chest feels tight, imagining she’s stopped breathing or that I’ll drop her, even when she’s right in my arms. I check the monitor every few minutes at night. There’s no real reason, but the worry just barges in and won’t leave.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes. It’s like a sudden wave—my heart races, I feel shaky, and I imagine something awful happening to the baby or that I’ll mess up somehow. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s happened a handful of times this week, and it leaves me exhausted.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. Feeding, laundry, trying to sleep—everything feels stacked up and heavier than it should. I still get through the basics, but by late afternoon I’m running on fumes and snapping at little things.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps circling through the day—worrying I didn’t burp her long enough, replaying every cry, picturing worst-case scenes. It takes me over an hour to settle, and when she finally sleeps I wake up every hour checking the monitor. I’m lucky if I get four broken hours a night.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, and it sticks around even when nothing “bad” is happening. Little moments of joy feel far away, like I’m watching life through a fogged window.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, a few times—mostly when I’m alone after she finally naps. Yesterday I just sat on the couch with cold coffee and cried because everything felt too heavy and I couldn’t explain why. It’s not all-day sobbing, but the tears come easily, maybe three or four evenings this week.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I feel low, but I haven’t thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum parent (≈ 1–2 wks post-delivery, per report)

Symptoms endorsed:
- Persistent low mood, “heavy/gray” daily  
- Marked anhedonia (rare, fleeting enjoyment; activities feel “chore-like”)  
- Daily crying spells, mostly evenings  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia related to rumination, monitor-checking  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Recurrent intrusive worries about infant safety; no objective basis  
- Panic-type episodes (tight chest, racing heart, “wave” sensation) several times/week  
- Sense of being overwhelmed by routine tasks, late-day irritability  

Safety: Denies self-harm or thoughts of harming infant.

Pattern: Symptoms present most days, interfere with functioning and rest; no prior psychiatric history reported.

Screening significance: High endorsement consistent with probable postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety features; moderate functional impairment. Recommends expedited formal evaluation (PHQ-9, GAD-7), psychoeducation, and safety-plan review.
